summary.title: Monoliths are the future
summary.one_liner: Kelsey Hightower argues that microservices often fail to solve the real problem, and that a poorly structured monolith split up often becomes a "distributed monolith" with more infrastructure but the same bad code.
takeaways: Microservices often do not address the real problem teams face, such as weak code discipline in a monolith.
Splitting a badly structured monolith can produce a distributed monolith: the same coupling, now over the network.
Splitting into services can add infrastructure needs like tracing and metrics, which can hide the original code problems.
A separate service can make sense when a new concern, such as mobile banking APIs, needs its own application that still connects to existing systems.
summary.summary: This is an excerpt from Go Time #114, where Kelsey Hightower shares an unpopular opinion that monoliths are the future. He argues that teams often move to microservices to fix poor engineering discipline, which only produces a distributed monolith with more deployables and more infrastructure. He gives a bank adding mobile banking as an example of when a separate service makes sense. The piece is a short, opinion-based excerpt in conversational form, with no code or benchmarks.
